fix: Class: delegating a merge decision to a check whose exit code means 'reported', not 'passed'. Call verdict-gate.py with --blocking, or refuse when the JSON verdict is "advisory" (keep "pass", and decide explicitly whether "not-judged"/predates qualify). Flip the 'gate advisory flagged' test case to a refusal. If merging under advisory is intended, that is Alex's call: say so in scope §4.3, because 'Done' under advisory is a much weaker bar than 'merged'.
text: run_gate treats verdict-gate.py exit 0 as the go-ahead, but the gate's default mode is advisory (verify_lib.GATE_MODE = "advisory"; no plans dir sets **Gate mode:**), where every block exits 0. Run now on this scope, `verdict-gate.py --unit 10.3 --json` prints verdict "advisory", "6 blocked — no final verdict", and exits 0. So a unit with no /verify verdict, a failed verify, undispositioned findings or unreviewed fix commits merges, with only a ticker marker. The test table locks this in: 'gate advisory flagged' expects a merge.

fix: Refuse merge when $HERDR_AGENT_NAME is set to anything other than "driver", whatever the --driver flag says (a named herdr agent that is not the driver is a lane), and add a test row: HERDR_AGENT_NAME=lane-x plus --driver is refused before gh. Keep --driver only for sessions outside herdr. Also correct the three docs to describe what is actually enforced.
text: 'Lanes never merge' rests only on packet.is_driver, which is true for any caller passing --driver. The documented command (plan/SKILL.md step 4) includes --driver, and lanes run /plan, so a lane that runs that step merges. A lane is identifiable: herdr sets $HERDR_AGENT_NAME to the lane name, yet a lane-named session passing --driver is still accepted. The docstring ('merge refuses a lane outright'), README ('refuses a lane before any gh call') and plan/SKILL.md:511 ('the script refuses it') all claim an enforcement the code does not have.

fix: Class: inferring why GitHub blocks from mergeStateStatus alone. Before using --admin, read the base branch's required checks (gh api repos/{slug}/branches/{base}/protection/required_status_checks, plus rulesets: gh api repos/{slug}/rules/branches/{base}). Require every required context to be present and SUCCESS in the rollup, and fail closed when protection is unreadable on a BLOCKED PR. Alternatively, admit --admin only when reviewDecision is REVIEW_REQUIRED and the required checks are satisfied.
text: BLOCKED → --admin bypasses every branch-protection rule, including required status checks that never reported. statusCheckRollup lists only contexts that have reported. A required check that never reports (a path-filtered workflow, a queued workflow not yet created, a renamed job) leaves the PR BLOCKED 'Expected — waiting for status'. cond_checks passes as long as some other check ran green, and --admin then merges past the missing required check. Scope §4.3 allows --admin 'under the same conditions', and 'CI is green with real runs' does not hold here.

fix: Compute the commits in merge-base..head, drop those touching only plans/, and require each remaining commit to sit inside some review record's base..head for this repo in the unit (or at least require the earliest review base to be an ancestor-or-equal of the merge-base). Refuse with the uncovered shas named. Add test rows for a pre-base code commit and a stacked branch.
text: covered() checks only the head end: that the review saw the PR head, or only plans/ changed after it. It never checks that the unit's reviews cover the PR's start. cond_verdict picks any review of this repo in the unit, so a PR whose merge-base..head contains commits before the review's base merges unreviewed. Examples: code committed before the ledger base was recorded, a stacked lane branch carrying another unit's commits, or a lane that ran two units on one branch with one PR.

fix: Treat a PR touching CI definitions (.github/workflows/, .github/actions/, CODEOWNERS, other repos' CI config) as not auto-mergeable: either add them to the floor in one-way-doors.defaults (a 10.1 surface, so record the decision) or add a driver-merge condition that refuses with a two-way packet.
text: 'Real green runs' is self-referential when the PR edits the CI that produces them: .github/workflows/ (and similar CI config) is not on the floor, so a PR that weakens or stubs its own test job (e.g. `run: true`) gets a real SUCCESS and merges to develop, which deploys to dev. An agent making its own CI pass is a known failure mode, and nothing here catches it.

fix: On a non-zero rc, run the same read-back (state, mergeCommit). If it reads MERGED with a merge commit, take the merged path (print MERGED, post the event, flag the gh error). Otherwise keep the refusal.
text: When gh pr merge exits non-zero, the PR is assumed unmerged without being read back. gh can exit non-zero after GitHub has merged (a network drop after the mutation, a post-merge step failing). The driver then prints NOT MERGED, writes a 'Not merged' packet asking someone to fix and re-run, and posts no `merged` event, though the PR landed. Task 3.2 says every merge posts an event.

fix: Either state in plan/SKILL.md and scope §4.3 that a repo with no CI always parks as a two-way packet, or give those repos a minimal real check. Don't relax the vacuous-green rule.
text: Docs say pmg-docs and ai-skills PRs merge to main, but neither repo has any CI workflow. cond_checks refuses an empty rollup as vacuous green, so the driver can never merge them (fail-closed, not unsafe). Scope §4.3's 'pmg-docs merge to main' is unreachable as built.

reason: CI definitions are now floor paths in scripts/one-way-doors.defaults (.github/workflows/, .github/actions/, CODEOWNERS, .circleci/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec*), so driver-merge's door check refuses a PR that edits its own CI; door tests per pattern

fix: Decide lane vs driver from something a lane actually carries. Inside herdr (HERDR_PANE_ID set), ask herdr for this pane's agent name over its socket/CLI and accept only `driver`. If the lookup fails, refuse (fail closed), and never fall back to --driver while HERDR_PANE_ID is set. Make --driver count only when no HERDR_* pane context exists. Replace the test's injected HERDR_AGENT_NAME with a case where only HERDR_PANE_ID is set plus --driver, and expect a refusal.
text: The r1-02 fix depends on herdr putting $HERDR_AGENT_NAME into a lane's environment, and nothing does that. New evidence: this review pane was launched by herdr (HERDR_PANE_ID, HERDR_TAB_ID, HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID and HERDR_SOCKET_PATH are all set) and $HERDR_AGENT_NAME is unset. Nothing in ai-skills (herdr/SKILL.md, herdr-pane.sh, concurrency/SKILL.md) sets it. Lanes are named with `herdr pane rename` / report-metadata, and the driver with `herdr agent rename $HERDR_PANE_ID driver` (herdr/SKILL.md:73). A rename after launch cannot change a running process's environment. So a real lane gets `name` == '' and falls through to pk.is_driver(a). The `--driver` in /plan's documented step-4 command then accepts it, which is exactly the r1-02 scenario. The real driver is in the same position: it also has no HERDR_AGENT_NAME and is a driver only because of --driver. Lane and driver are still indistinguishable. The test 'lane with --driver refused before gh' passes only because it injects HERDR_AGENT_NAME=lane-x, a state production does not produce. plan/SKILL.md:516-518 and the docstring now describe a protection that does not fire for real lanes.

fix: Read `state,mergeCommit,headRefOid` back. Treat it as this merge only when headRefOid == facts['head']. Otherwise report it as merged, but not by this run at the checked head: no `merged` event, or one flagged with the actual head. Add a test with merge_rc=1 and a read-back MERGED at a different head.
text: The r1-06 read-back after a non-zero `gh pr merge` reads only `state,mergeCommit`, and any MERGED is treated as this merge. --match-head-commit guarantees the merged head only when gh succeeded. On the failure path, gh may have failed because the head moved (a lane pushed an unreviewed commit) or for any other reason, and the PR may then have been merged by someone else or at a different head. The driver still prints MERGED with the read-back sha and posts a `merged` event claiming it merged the reviewed head. That event covers commits no condition checked.

fix: Carry (context, app_id/integration_id) from both protection sources. Require a SUCCESS CheckRun from that app when an app is bound (the rollup's CheckRun carries checkSuite.app, or read check-runs for the head). When the binding cannot be verified, refuse --admin.
text: The --admin precondition from r1-03 matches required checks by name only. A SUCCESS from any source with that name counts. The code ignores the classic protection's `checks[].app_id` and the ruleset's `integration_id`, which are GitHub's binding of a required check to the app that must report it, and --admin then bypasses GitHub's own enforcement of that binding. Any token with commit-status write access can post a StatusContext `e2e`=success on the head, for example `gh api repos/o/r/statuses/<sha> -f context=e2e -f state=success`. That turns a required check that never reported (the r1-03 scenario) into an --admin merge. Agents making their own CI pass is the failure mode r1-05 named.

fix: Keep the floor for irreversible changes. Give driver-merge its own 'never auto-merge' path list (CI definitions) as a separate condition that writes a two-way packet ('Alex reviews the CI change and merges by hand'). Revert the defaults lines and move their door tests to driver-merge's table.
text: The r1-05 fix widens the global one-way-door floor, but this floor is not merge-only. door.py also reads it for /concurrency and /plan §6.9 packet promotion (a lane's two-way packet whose --range touches .github/workflows/ now goes out one-way and parks the lane) and for /review case-1 reframe packets. Editing CI is reversible, and the file's own contract (line 3) says a hit 'makes the change one-way'. So every unit that adds or edits a workflow now parks on a door that is not one. That includes adding CI to pmg-docs/ai-skills, which r1-07's note implies is the path to auto-merge. The refusal packet also offers 'Rework the PR off the floor' (driver-merge.py:439) for a CI edit.

fix: Either accept SKIPPED/NEUTRAL for a required check that is present in the rollup (absence stays a refusal), or document that skipped required checks always park.
text: Only SUCCESS counts as a satisfied required check. GitHub accepts a required check that concluded SKIPPED or NEUTRAL (a job skipped by `if:`) as passing. A BLOCKED PR whose only block is reviews, with a required job skipped by `if:`, is refused --admin and parks. This fails closed, but it will produce packets for PRs that are fine.

fix: Use `gh api --paginate`, or refuse when the response holds exactly per_page entries.
text: The rulesets read is one page (per_page=100, no --paginate). A branch with more than 100 active rules would drop the required_status_checks rules past page 1, and the missing checks would read as not required. That is unlikely at this scale, but it is a fail-open path in a function whose docstring promises unreadable is never read as 'nothing required'.

fix: A required (name, app) is satisfied only when at least one entry exists and EVERY rollup or check-run entry matching it is satisfied. Any non-satisfied entry of a required name means not satisfied. Add a test with a SUCCESS check run and a FAILURE status of the same required context, and one with two same-app runs where one fails, both expecting no --admin.
text: Satisfied requires only that SOME entry of a required name is satisfied. green is the set of names with any SUCCESS/SKIPPED/NEUTRAL rollup entry, and by_app (line 340) is the same per (name, app). A FAILURE or PENDING entry of the same name is therefore ignored. GitHub's rule differs: when a check run and a commit status share a required name, both are required. The check-runs endpoint can also return several latest runs of one name from one app across check suites, for example a workflow triggered on both push and pull_request for the same head. If one of those fails or is still pending, GitHub reports BLOCKED, and this code reads the BLOCKED as 'only reviews block' and merges with --admin past the failing required check. That is the r1-03 class (--admin past a required check that has not passed), now on the r2-05 satisfied() line. Note also: this is the fourth round in which the --admin precondition draws findings (r1-03, r2-03, r2-05, r2-06, now this). Re-deriving GitHub's protection evaluation client-side to justify a bypass is itself the convergence signal; narrowing --admin (e.g. only when the PR's sole unmet requirement is review approval, read from the GraphQL reviewDecision, with every rollup entry of every required name satisfied) or dropping it is the user's call.

fix: Stop identifying the driver by a name any session can set. Identify lanes from a record the lane does not write. /concurrency already logs each lane's pane in dispatch-log.py (--pane). driver_identity would refuse a pane with an open dispatch record and otherwise honour --driver, with --pane made required at dispatch. Failing that, at minimum gate plan §5.8.1's rename to non-lane sessions and remove the rename command from the refusal bullet.
text: The r2-01 fix makes the driver whichever pane herdr names `driver`, but that name is self-assigned, and the shipped workflow tells /plan sessions to assign it. plan/SKILL.md:362 (§5.8.1) says any /plan running in a herdr pane with a Primary repo runs `herdr agent rename "$HERDR_PANE_ID" driver`. Nothing in that step excludes lanes, and this code's own premise (driver_identity's docstring and r1-02) is that lanes run /plan. So a lane running /plan Phase 0 names itself `driver`, and both driver-merge.py's `driver` condition and packet.py's POST gate then accept it. plan/SKILL.md:521-522 makes it worse: the bullet that explains a lane's refusal prints the exact rename command, next to the instruction to fix the failed condition and re-run. Nothing checks that only one pane is named driver, and herdr/SKILL.md:62 says Alex usually runs two drivers, so uniqueness cannot be the rule anyway. This is the r1-02 -> r2-01 defect a third time: lane and driver are told apart by a label the lane can give itself. The impact is bounded, because every PR-level condition (review, gate, CI, floor, mergeable) still has to hold. A lane merge therefore lands an eligible PR out of the driver's sequence, not an unchecked one, so this is should-fix and not blocking. Round 3: this is a design problem, not a patch gap (see reframe).

fix: Give the elsewhere packet its own id kind. One option is stable_id('merge-elsewhere', label, merged_sha[:12]), keyed on the merge commit that landed. Another is to include the title in the id parts. Add a test: a refusal on head H, then a MERGED-ELSEWHERE read-back on H, must produce a second distinct packet.
text: The MERGED-ELSEWHERE packet added for r2-02 (driver-merge.py:668-673) goes through emit_packet. Its id is stable_id('merge', label, head[:12], door), and title and options are not part of the id. A refusal packet from an earlier run on the same checked head has the same id. Re-running driver-merge after a two-way refusal (checks pending, UNSTABLE, BEHIND) is the documented path. When packet.py new receives an existing --id (packet.py:417-421), it re-sends the OLD packet document: 'existing packet re-sent: idempotent on id'. So when a re-run finds the PR merged past the checked head, Alex gets the earlier 'Not merged: driver fixes the failed condition' card again, or nothing if that card was already answered. He never gets 'Merged past the checked head: review the commits merged unchecked'. The one case that most needs a human (unreviewed commits on the base) has its notice suppressed. The `merged` event is correctly withheld, so nothing else surfaces it.

fix: Print driver_identity's detail whenever --driver was passed but refused, at both :484 and :627, and make flush exit non-zero in that case. Rename the driver unconditionally in §5.8.1 (any herdr /plan driver), not only when a Primary repo is set. The reframe removes this too, because an unrenamed driver is not in the dispatch log.
text: This is a POST regression. Before this range, --driver made a session a driver everywhere (HERDR_AGENT_NAME was never set). Inside herdr, --driver is now ignored, so only a pane renamed `driver` POSTs. That rename happens only in plan §5.8.1, and only when the scope's Primary repo is not 'none' (plan/SKILL.md:360-361). A driver for a docs scope with Primary repo 'none', or a driver session that did not start through /plan Phase 0, is now silently not a driver. Its packets stay in the outbox, driver-merge refuses it, and the exit-4 recovery 'run packet.py flush --driver' prints 'flush: not a driver; nothing sent' and returns. Both messages (here and the new-packet note at :484, 'lane writes the outbox') drop driver_identity's detail. A driver that passed --driver is told it is a lane, and is never told why or that a herdr rename is needed.

fix: Narrow the wording to 'a PR editing a CI definition file (CI_DEFINITIONS)'. Note that scripts the workflows invoke are covered by the review, not by this condition.
text: The docstring says a PR editing the CI that produced its own green never auto-merges, but CI_DEFINITIONS (line 94) lists only the workflow, action and pipeline files. A workflow step `run: ./scripts/ci.sh` or `make test` makes the green depend on files outside the list, so editing them is the same self-referential green and still auto-merges. This is reasonable because the review range covers those edits, but the claim overstates the guarantee. A nested `sub/.github/workflows/` is also not matched (prefix glob), though GitHub only runs root workflows, so that one is harmless.

deletes: packet.py herdr_agent_name (the `herdr agent list` subprocess, HERDR_TIMEOUT, lru_cache, JSON parse and pane-count paths), the herdr-name branch of driver_identity, the `herdr agent rename … driver` dependency in plan/SKILL.md step 4's lane bullet, and tests/_helpers.py fake_herdr
proposal: Identify lanes, not the driver. /concurrency already records each lane's pane id in dispatch-log.py when it dispatches; make --pane required there. driver_identity would refuse any pane with an open dispatch record (the driver writes that record, not the lane) and otherwise honour --driver as before r2-01. This record cannot be self-assigned by a session following /plan, and an unrenamed driver keeps POSTing.

fix: Fail closed on anything not modelled. required_checks already pages /rules/branches. Refuse --admin when any rule there has a type other than required_status_checks or pull_request, or a pull_request rule sets required_review_thread_resolution. For classic protection, read /branches/{b}/protection and refuse when required_signatures, required_conversation_resolution or required_deployments (or lock_branch) are enabled. An unreadable response is no --admin. Alternatively, Alex drops --admin: BLOCKED becomes a two-way packet and he merges by hand. Given the convergence, that is the recommendation.
text: --admin still merges past branch protection that is not a review or a required check. reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED says a review approval is missing. It does not say that is the only thing missing. required_checks (line 281) reads only the required_status_checks rule from classic protection and from rulesets. Any other requirement that also holds BLOCKED is bypassed by --admin and never read: unresolved conversations (classic required_conversation_resolution, or the ruleset pull_request rule's required_review_thread_resolution), required signatures, required deployments, ruleset code_scanning / workflows / merge_queue. Example: a PR needs a review and has an unresolved review thread. GitHub reports BLOCKED + REVIEW_REQUIRED, every required check is green, cond_mergeable returns admin=True, and the merge goes through. So the docstring at :337 and plan/SKILL.md:508 ('only when GitHub says the missing piece is a review approval') overclaim, and Alex 83's premise ('review approval is the only unmet requirement') is not what the code checks. This is the fifth round in a row where the --admin precondition draws a finding (r1-03, r2-03, r2-05, r2-06, r3-01). Rebuilding GitHub's protection evaluation on the client to justify a bypass keeps leaking.

fix: Defect to fix: drop the remediation command from the lane-facing message. Say 'the driver closes this record when the lane ends; a lane never merges, do not re-run'. In plan §the merge step, exclude the driver condition from 'fix the condition and re-run'. Residual for Alex to accept: a same-user file cannot stop a lane that deliberately writes to it. Only an OS or account boundary could, for example the driver holding the log under a different user.
text: A lane can still pass as the driver, and the refusal tells it how. The r3-02 mechanism comes back on the fix's own lines. The dispatch log is a plain file in ~/.config owned by the same user every lane runs as (lanes run with --dangerously-skip-permissions), and dispatch-log.py has no caller check. So the docstring's claim at :214-216 ('never by the lane, so a lane cannot take it off itself') is false: the lane appends one line and it is out. The refusal text driver-merge prints in its `driver` row ends with 'if that lane is finished, record it with dispatch-log.py --pane <id> --status done — lanes never merge'. plan/SKILL.md:517-518 tells whoever ran driver-merge, on NOT MERGED, to 'fix the condition and re-run'. A lane running /plan's merge step gets both lines together and follows them: it closes its own record, re-runs, and merges. Impact is still bounded as in r3-02, because every PR-level condition must hold.

fix: Invert the filter so it fails closed: skip a record only when its machine is a KNOWN other host (homelab2026, or the accounts map's machine list), and count any unknown value as this machine. Alternatively, make dispatch-log.py reject a --machine that is not this host or a known remote (it can call placement.this_host). Add a test with an alias machine value.
text: A free-text machine mismatch silently turns a lane into a driver. A record counts only when its `machine` is blank or exactly equals socket.gethostname() short-lowercased. `--machine` is typed by the driver from the plan's `machine=<host>` and is never validated by dispatch-log.py. The live log already holds 36 records with machine 'mba' while this host is 'ak-mba2025' (168 use the hostname). A lane logged with an alias, or with a different case/FQDN form of hostname -s (placement.py uses `hostname -s`, this uses socket.gethostname), is skipped. It then reads as 'no open dispatch record' and is accepted as a driver. The machine filter exists so another server's pane ids are ignored, but it fails open on any spelling it does not recognise.

fix: Residual Alex should accept knowingly, or invert. To accept: rewrite plan :524 as 'a pane logged as a lane never merges; an unlogged pane is treated as the driver', and require a dispatch-log record for every review and fix pane the driver opens. To invert: the driver registers its own pane (a `driver` record) and only a registered pane passes. That fails closed for helpers, at the cost r3-04 named (an unregistered driver must be told why).
text: 'A /concurrency lane never merges' overstates what the dispatch-log rule gives. The default flipped. Under r2, any pane not named `driver` was a lane, so it failed closed. Now any herdr pane with no open dispatch record is a driver whenever it passes --driver, which fails open. That covers every pane the driver spawns outside /concurrency §6 step 4: review and fix rounds, /research lanes, herdr-pane.sh helper splits, and a dispatch whose log write was skipped or failed. Evidence: this review pane (w14:p3M) has 0 records in the log, so `driver-merge.py merge --driver` here would pass the driver condition. concurrency/SKILL.md:228-229 admits this ('A lane you launch without logging it ... can POST and merge as a driver'). The plan text a lane actually reads does not.

fix: Delete OPEN_LANE, or define CLOSED = ('done', 'failed') and use it in open_dispatch.
text: OPEN_LANE = ('dispatched', 'blocked') is never read. open_dispatch hard-codes ('done', 'failed') as closed and treats every other status as open. The constant documents a rule the code does not use, and a later edit to it changes nothing.

fix: When a new refusal id is minted for a label+head that already has an outbox packet with a different id, mark the earlier one stale (packet.py stale), or say in the body that it supersedes the earlier one.
text: The refusal packet id now includes a hash of the failed condition names. Re-running on the same head with a different failure set (checks pending, then UNSTABLE, then BLOCKED) now mints a new card each time, while the earlier card for the same PR and head stays open in the queue. That fixes r3-03 (the old card is no longer re-sent), but Alex can hold several open cards for one PR, most of them stale.

deletes: cond_mergeable's BLOCKED branch (reviewDecision gate, required_checks, entry_ok, the check-runs app-binding read) and the --admin flag in merge()
proposal: Drop --admin entirely. Merge only when GitHub says CLEAN or HAS_HOOKS. Any BLOCKED becomes a two-way packet and Alex merges by hand, the same path a repo with no CI already takes.
